title: Accountant Cost Per Lead 2026: Click Prices and Budgets
summary: An accountant click costs $24.52 on average in the US. See cost per lead at 5% to 15% conversion, Google vs LSA vs Facebook, and monthly budgets.
body_markdown:
## The short answer


- In the US, a click on 'accountant' averages $24.52, and clicks on 'tax preparation' and 'tax preparer' average $14.45 each. A click on 'cpa near me' averages $12.72.
- At a 10% click-to-lead rate, those clicks work out to about $245, $145 and $127 per lead. At 5% the same clicks cost twice as much per lead.
- Facebook and Instagram leads are cheaper on paper. LocaliQ's 2026 all-industry figure is $27.39 per Meta lead against $66.69 per Google Search lead, but the intent is different.
- A starting budget formula: new clients you want per month, divided by the share of leads that become clients, times your cost per lead.


## What a click costs


Accounting is one of the pricier searches on Google. Here is what the main searches cost in the US.


Search US searches a month Average click Top-of-page range


accountant 110,000 $24.52 $7.46 to $30.35


tax preparation 33,100 $14.45 $4.96 to $25.90


cpa near me 90,500 $12.72 $4.32 to $24.27


tax preparer 33,100 $14.45 $4.96 to $25.90


The range is wide because the buyer is not always the same. Urgency pushes bids up: someone with a deadline or a notice wants an answer now, and firms pay for that moment. Competition matters too, since many firms and national tax chains bid on the same words. City matters most of all: the same search costs far more in a crowded metro than in a small town, which is why the top-of-page range runs from $4.32 to $30.35 across these searches.


## From click to cost per lead


A click is not a lead. Cost per lead is the click price divided by the share of clicks that become a call or a form. Here is the math for 'accountant' at its $24.52 average click, with a worked example for new clients.


Click-to-lead rate Cost per lead Cost per new client if 1 in 3 leads books (example)


5% $490 $1,471


10% $245 $736


15% $163 $490


The math is $24.52 divided by 0.05, 0.10 and 0.15, then multiplied by 3 for the last column. The 1 in 3 booking rate is an example, not a benchmark. Plug in your own click price, conversion rate and booking rate with the[cost per lead calculator](https://www.sprites.ai/tools/cost-per-lead-calculator) .


## Google Ads vs Local Services Ads vs Facebook for accountants and tax preparers


Google Ads (Search) Local Services Ads Facebook and Instagram


How you pay Per click Per lead, with the price set by Google by category and area Per impression or click, with leads from a form


Intent High: the buyer is searching for an accountant now High: the buyer is looking for a local provider Lower: the buyer is scrolling, not searching


When it wins for this trade You want clients with a need today, such as a tax filing, a notice or a new business setup, and you can handle expensive clicks Your category and area are offered and you want to pay only for leads. Availability varies, so check before planning around it You sell planned services such as bookkeeping, payroll or year-round advisory, or want to fill the calendar before a busy period


For context, LocaliQ's 2026 figures for business services show a Google Search cost per lead of $93.69, an average click of $5.87 and a conversion rate of 4.85%. Those are business services figures, not accountant figures. A $24.52 click on 'accountant' is more than four times that $5.87 average, and even 'cpa near me' at $12.72 is more than double it, so expect accountant leads to cost more than the benchmark. Across all industries, LocaliQ's 2026 figures are $66.69 per Google Search lead and $27.39 per Meta lead. See the[average cost per lead by industry](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/average-cost-per-lead-by-industry) for more comparisons.


Google charges per lead in Local Services Ads and sets the price by category and area, so there is no number to quote here. Our guide to[Google Local Services Ads](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/google-local-services-ads) explains how they work and how to check what is offered in your area.


## How much to spend each month


Work backwards from the clients you want.


1. Pick the number of new clients you want per month.
2. Divide by your booking rate (the share of leads that become clients) to get the leads you need.
3. Multiply the leads by your cost per lead.


Example inputs: you want 5 new clients a month, 1 in 3 leads becomes a client, and your cost per lead is $245 (a $24.52 click at a 10% conversion rate). You need 5 divided by one third, which is 15 leads. At $245 each, that is $3,675 a month.


Start on one channel. Run it long enough to see your real click price, conversion rate and booking rate, then change the budget or add a second channel. Our[guide to tax preparer advertising](https://www.sprites.ai/blog/tax-preparer-advertising) covers what to run first.


## How to lower your cost per lead


- **Lead with a specific offer.** A free first consultation, a flat-fee tax return or a fixed-price bookkeeping setup gives people a reason to act now.
- **Match the landing page to the search.** Someone searching 'tax preparer' should land on a page about tax preparation with a phone number and a short form, not on your home page.
- **Answer every call and form fast.** A missed call goes to the next firm on the list. Use a call-back text or a staffed line so leads are not wasted.
- **Add negative keywords.** Block searches like 'accountant jobs', 'accounting degree', 'free tax software' and 'accountant salary' so you do not pay for clicks from people who are not buyers.
- **Set a tight service area.** Target the towns and zip codes you actually serve, since the same search costs far more in some cities than others.
- **Keep the lead form short.** Ask for name, phone and the service they need. Each extra field loses people, but one qualifying question, such as personal or business, saves wasted calls.
